hints: A project can follow another only when its end time is no later than the next start.
Sort projects by end time and find the last compatible project for each one.
Dynamic programming compares skipping a project with taking its reward plus the best compatible prefix.
analogy: For each project, either ignore it or add it after the best schedule that finished before it starts.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
algorithm: Sort projects by end time. For project i, binary-search p(i), the last earlier project with end<start[i]; set dp[i]=max(dp[i-1],reward[i]+dp[p(i)]).
correctness: An optimal schedule either excludes project i or includes it; in the latter case all earlier chosen projects must end strictly before i starts, exactly the prefix represented by p(i).
example: Projects ending at time 4 and starting at time 4 cannot both be selected; compatibility requires the earlier project to finish strictly before the next starts.
